info.name: Referalli API
info.description:
Attribution-first affiliate and referral platform. Everything the dashboards do, this API does.

## Authentication
Server-side, send an API key: `Authorization: Bearer rk_live_…` (or `rk_test_…` for test mode). A key holds scopes (`full`, `read`, or per resource such as `referrals:write`); each operation names the scope it needs. Browser calls from your own front end use a publishable key (`rk_pub_…`, limited to `programs:read` and `events:write` from allowed origins). The dashboards and the partner portal use session cookies.

## Versions
Every request runs under an API version: the `referalli-version` header (the name from before the rename is still accepted), else the key's pinned version, else 2026-10-21. The latest is 2026-11-01; list operations return the paginated envelope `{ object: "list", data, has_more, next_cursor }` from 2026-11-01. A version stays supported for at least 12 months after the next one ships. Deprecated versions are announced in the changelog and in a `referalli-deprecation` response header at least 6 months before they stop being served. API keys keep their pinned version until you change it.

## Test mode
Test keys, or `referalli-mode: test` on a session, act on the org's separate test data.

## Errors
Every error is `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details"?, "requestId"?, "docs_url" } }`; branch on `code`. Writes accept an `Idempotency-Key` header for safe retries.

## Webhooks
Each event topic and its payload is in the `webhooks` section of this document.

Generated from the OpenAPI document (version 2026-11-01). Set `apiKey` to an API key; `baseUrl` defaults to production.

item.name: Receive an OpenID Connect back-channel logout

request.description:
The `backchannel_logout_uri` of Referalli's own sign-in client. Takes a form-encoded `logout_token` (OpenID Connect Back-Channel Logout 1.0): verified against the issuer's keys, `aud`, `events`, a fresh `iat`, no `nonce`, and a single-use `jti`; then ends the Referalli sessions for its `sid` (or every session of its `sub`). Answers 503 until the deployment sets IDP_LOGOUT_SYNC=true.

**Auth:** none.

Ends the browser session (and any portal-domain sessions handed off from it) and clears the cookies. Returns the identity provider's `logoutUrl` to end the provider session too, or `null`.

item.name: Start sign-in with an org's own identity provider

request.description:
Team single sign-on with the merchant's OWN identity provider (OpenID Connect or WorkOS), no broker. `org` names the organization; sets the flow cookie and redirects (302) to its IdP. `link=1` from a signed-in user links the IdP identity to that user instead of creating an account (accounts are never linked by email). Problems redirect to `/login?error=`.

**Auth:** none.

item.name: Start partner sign-in with the merchant's identity provider

request.description:
Partner-portal sign-in through the merchant's own OpenID Connect IdP (portal sign-in adapter `oidc`). On the merchant's verified portal domain the flow runs on Referalli's host and is handed back. Problems redirect to `/portal/login?error=`.

**Auth:** none.

item.name: Complete sign-in with an org's own identity provider

request.description:
The redirect URI to register at the merchant's IdP, for team SSO and partner-portal OIDC. Verifies `state`, exchanges `code`, verifies the ID token (issuer, audience, nonce, asymmetric signature), resolves the identity `<adapter>:<issuer hash>:<sub>` and, for the team, sets the role the IdP's groups map to (never owner). Failures redirect to the login page with `?error=` (`sso_no_role`, `email_taken`, `invalid_token`…).

**Auth:** none.

item.name: Sign a partner in with the merchant's token

request.description:
"Bring your own session" (portal sign-in adapter `custom`): the merchant's backend sends the partner's browser here with `token`, a JWT signed with an asymmetric key from its JWKS, `aud` `referalli:<orgId>`, its configured `iss`, `sub`, `email`, and `exp - iat` ≤ 300 s. Each token works once. Creates or finds the partner account by `jwt:<issuer hash>:<sub>` (never by email), links or enrolls the partner in the org, sets the session and redirects to `next` or `/portal`.

**Auth:** none.
